readiness.no-product-body: Readiness audits a product's structure: without knowing what you sell, at what price and to whom, there is nothing to audit.
readiness.intro-body: Cheap paid traffic doesn't come from cheap clicks — it comes from a structure that converts. Tick what's already done below: blockers show up instantly, for free. The full verdict tells you what to fix first and why.
readiness.checklist-body: Tick only what you're sure about. Anything left unticked is treated as “not confirmed” — never as missing.
readiness.group-why-mensuracao: Without a reliable signal the algorithm can't learn, the learning phase never closes and cost per result stays high. It's the cheapest thing to fix and the most expensive to ignore.
readiness.group-why-pagina: After the click, the page is what converts. Every point of conversion here cuts your cost per sale by the same proportion.
readiness.group-why-checkout: It's the last metre before the money lands. Friction and missing payment methods kill the sale after you've already paid for the click.
readiness.group-why-descoberta: Being found outside of ads reduces dependence on paid media and makes acquisition cheaper over time.
readiness.group-why-funil: Whoever didn't buy today may still buy. Without capture and follow-up, you pay again for the same visitor.

readiness.item-events-pixelInstalled: It depends on your model. Selling a one-off product (course, ebook, physical item)? Tick Initiate Checkout and Purchase — and Add to Cart if your checkout has that step. Selling by subscription or a trial period? Tick Complete Registration, Start Trial and Subscribe instead. The rest of the list only matters if your site actually has that specific feature.
readiness.item-parameters-pixelInstalled: The fields marked "Required parameter" are already ticked and locked — you can't uncheck them, so ignore them. Among the optional ones, prioritize Email, Phone and the two cookie fields (fbc and fbp): those raise event-match quality the most. First name, last name and postal code help a bit more. The rest (birthday, gender, subscription ID...) are only worth it if you actually collect that data — never tick a field your site can't fill in.
readiness.intake-reassure: Not sure what something is? Leave it unticked and hit “I don't know what this is” — we'll explain. Nothing here is required.

readiness.na-reason-platform-owns-site: This belongs to the platform's site, not to a page of your own.
readiness.na-reason-no-own-server: This needs your own server, which you don't have in this selling format.

readiness.item-what-pixelInstalled: A small piece of Meta code on your site. It tells Facebook/Instagram who visited and who bought — without it, the ad cannot learn who your customer is.
readiness.item-what-conversionEventTested: Testing whether the “sale completed” signal actually fires when someone buys. Having the code installed does not guarantee it works.
readiness.item-what-capiInstalled: A second signalling path that leaves from your server instead of the browser. It keeps you from losing sales when the browser blocks tracking.
readiness.item-what-analyticsInstalled: A tool that shows how many people entered your site, where they came from and what they did. Google Analytics (GA4) is the most common and it is free.
readiness.item-what-pageHasProof: Testimonials, customer photos, numbers or real cases on your page. It answers the “can I trust this?” of someone who does not know you.
readiness.item-what-pageMobileTested: Opening your own page on a phone and buying as if you were a customer. Most ad traffic comes from phones.
readiness.item-what-pageFast: Your page opening in a few seconds. A slow page makes people leave before seeing the offer — and you already paid for the click.
readiness.item-what-hasGuarantee: A clear refund promise (e.g. 7 days). It lowers the fear of buying from someone you don't know yet.
readiness.item-what-paymentPix: Accepting PIX. In Brazil it is the most used method; not having it usually costs sales.
readiness.item-what-paymentCard: Accepting credit card, including instalments when they make sense for your ticket.
readiness.item-what-checkoutShort: Asking for as little data as possible to close the sale. Every extra field costs conversion.
readiness.item-what-abandonedRecovery: An automatic reminder (email or WhatsApp) for whoever started buying and did not finish.
readiness.item-what-seoBasics: The title and description that show up on Google when someone finds your site. They are two short texts inside the page.
readiness.item-what-indexable: Letting Google show your site in results. Sometimes a site is born blocked by mistake and nobody notices.
readiness.item-what-sitemapRobots: Two files that help Google understand your site. Whoever built the site usually created them.
readiness.item-what-structuredData: Extra markup that tells Google what each thing is (product, price, rating). It helps you show up better in search.
readiness.item-what-socialProfiles: Having active profiles on the networks where your audience is, with your site link in the bio.
readiness.item-what-organicContent: Publishing with some regularity. Being found without paying reduces your dependence on ads over time.
readiness.item-what-emailCapture: A way to capture the contact of someone who visits and does not buy — email, WhatsApp or phone.
readiness.item-what-emailFollowup: A sequence of messages for whoever left their contact but has not bought yet.
readiness.item-what-remarketingAudience: An audience built from people who already visited your site, so you can advertise again only to them.
readiness.item-hire-pixelInstalled: Install the Meta Pixel on every page of my site and set up the standard events (view, initiate checkout and purchase), testing that each one fires.
readiness.item-hire-conversionEventTested: Validate in Meta Events Manager that the purchase event really fires on every sale, without duplication.
readiness.item-hire-capiInstalled: Set up Meta's Conversions API server-side, with deduplication against the Pixel.
readiness.item-hire-analyticsInstalled: Install Google Analytics 4 on the site and set up purchase tracking.
readiness.item-hire-pageFast: Optimise page load speed (images, scripts and caching).
readiness.item-hire-checkoutShort: Reduce checkout fields and steps to the minimum necessary.
readiness.item-hire-abandonedRecovery: Set up automatic abandoned-cart recovery by email and/or WhatsApp.
readiness.item-hire-indexable: Check and enable the site's indexing on Google (meta robots and robots.txt).
readiness.item-hire-sitemapRobots: Publish a correct sitemap.xml and robots.txt and submit the sitemap to Google Search Console.
readiness.item-hire-structuredData: Implement product and organisation structured data (schema.org) on the site.
readiness.item-hire-remarketingAudience: Create the remarketing audience in Ads Manager from the site Pixel.
readiness.creative-plan-hint: Angle and hook hypotheses to test organically before paying for media.
readiness.funnel-model-hint: This changes what we audit. Where payment happens decides which items make sense for your business — and which do not.
readiness.funnel-model-why-direct: People click the ad, land on the page and buy right there. The checkout is public.
readiness.funnel-model-why-trial_first: People sign up (free or trial), use the product and only then decide to pay. The checkout sits AFTER login.
readiness.funnel-model-why-lead_first: People leave their contact and someone on the team closes the sale. There is no self-service checkout.
readiness.group-why-ativacao: In your model the money arrives after login. What decides the outcome is how many signups become paying customers — not how many signups you get.
readiness.item-what-signupFrictionLow: This is your top-of-funnel “checkout”: every extra field drops the rate of people who get in. Ask for the minimum needed to start, and collect the rest later inside the product.
readiness.item-what-activationDefined: The action that shows someone understood the value (the “aha”) — creating their first record, for example. Without defining and measuring it you cannot tell a good signup from one that will never pay.
readiness.item-what-trialToPaidTracked: Knowing how many signups become paying customers, and how long it takes. It is the most important number in your model: since the ad optimizes for signups, without it you scale the cheapest signup instead of the customer who pays.
readiness.item-hire-trialToPaidTracked: I need to measure my product's trial-to-paid conversion: identify the source (campaign/ad) of each signup, link that signup to the paid subscription when it happens, and send that purchase event to Meta via the Conversions API using the same identifier as the signup.
readiness.item-upgradePathClear: Clear upgrade path inside the product
readiness.item-what-upgradePathClear: People can subscribe without hunting for it or talking to anyone: the subscribe button is visible during use and the price is clear before the click.
readiness.na-reason-sales-closes-deal: In your model a person on the team closes the sale, so there is no self-service checkout to adjust.
readiness.na-reason-no-trial: This item only makes sense for businesses with a signup/trial before the purchase.
readiness.blocker-trial-conversion-unmeasured: trial → paid conversion is not measured — since the ad optimizes for signups, the algorithm will scale the cheapest signup, not the customer who pays
